soundness_flags.label: ass:uniform-bridge-product-rate / thm:postselection-wald
soundness_flags.one_line: The condition labelled standard is a product of two strong L2 bridge errors, whereas ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 uses a weak-metric/strong-metric product for its fixed-system CLT; this instrumental strengthening must be replaced by a designwise uniform version of the published condition or retagged and independently justified.

soundness_flags.label: ass:unique-outcome-bridge and ass:operator-bijectivity
soundness_flags.one_line: For the stated operator, bijectivity already makes the observed outcome-bridge equation have a unique L2 solution whenever it has one, so retaining a separate unique-outcome-bridge assumption is redundant.

soundness_flags.label: thm:pilot-oracle-regret
soundness_flags.one_line: “A positive oracle gap” is not defined: introduce a scalar separation such as min_{d notin d*(P)}[V_d^*(P)-min_{d'}V_{d'}^*(P)] (with an explicit empty-set convention) before asserting selection consistency.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 8 distinguishes weak operator-metric and strong L2 errors; Theorem 5 requires a product involving one weak and one strong error, Theorem 4 is consistency, and Theorem 7 identifies the local efficiency bound under unique bridges and bijective T.
Under random assignment and homoskedasticity, the paper rewrites its fixed-trial MSE/power design problem as residual prediction variance divided by sample size under a budget.
The paper derives an ATE semiparametric efficiency bound with limited outcomes and compares fixed surrogate-observation settings.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v2, 2022; corroborating accessible version of the later Management Science article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work studies long-term-outcome targeting via imputed outcomes and reports that its approach outperforms a policy learned from short-term proxies; it does not establish a bridge-efficiency approximation theorem.
The paper studies online moment selection with costed sources, estimated oracle allocations, and zero asymptotic-MSE regret.
The paper derives semiparametric-efficiency-based two-phase sampling rules and analyzes estimation of the optimal rule.
The paper treats asymptotically normal inference for strongly identified functionals of weakly identified conditional-moment nuisances using penalized minimax estimation.
The paper studies regularized linear surrogate indices with many noisy proxies and compares them to naive screening, not persistent-confounding bridge-design efficiency ratios.
The paper derives a closed-form cost-aware sampling policy and estimator for multivariate additive-noise linear front-door/back-door models.

Define an oracle separation scalar and use it consistently in the pilot-selection theorem, including its tie convention and a finite-sample mis-selection bound in terms of that scalar and the pilot variance-estimation error.
